goalsQuestion: What message traffic, latency and delivery time should I use?
constraintsQuestion: What acknowledgement, ordering, retry and retention guarantees should I support?
requirementsAnswer: I will estimate message throughput from the discussed daily volume and ten-times peak factor, target p95 acceptance below 200 milliseconds and online delivery below 1 second, and retain private conversation history for 90 days.
coreExplanation: The messaging API checks that the sender is a participant, stores the conversation ID, sender, client-generated send ID and body durably, and acknowledges only after that write; history uses a cursor over stored messages.
Each conversation has a sequencer that assigns increasing message IDs, and a unique constraint on sender and client send ID makes retries return the original message rather than storing it twice.
validationExplanation: Connected devices receive new messages; after a disconnect they request history after their last confirmed message ID, and each device deduplicates displayed IDs.
If a delivery worker fails, another can replay durable undelivered work; I would measure delivery lag, failed sends and backlog, load-test reconnect bursts, and purge messages after 90 days.
weakAnswer: I acknowledge messages before saving them and keep them only in the sender's live connection. Every retry creates a new message, and any signed-in user can request any conversation.
reviewFocus: Live connections alone cannot provide durable acceptance or offline history.
A retry creating another logical message contradicts send idempotency.
Signing in does not authorize access to every conversation.
